newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease 0.59 pct, off lows on support.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease 0.59 pct, off lows on support.

text.p: Istanbul shares maintained their downwards trend in thin volume on Friday, but rebounded from lows on fresh support at the index's 1,480 mark after the breaking of 1,500 support in the morning, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,505, down nine points, or 0.59 percent, from Thursday, but up from a late low of 1,483. Volume fell further to 14.13 trillion lira from Thursday's 17.49 trillion.
Over the week, the index lost 4.1 percent after last week's 1.2 percent gain.

"The index maintained its downtrend and movement within tight bands. The 1,480 support held today. The market is nervous because of a National Security Council meeting due at the end of April. The (political) outlook is not clear," said Haydar Haydaroglu from Halk securities.
Investors diverting their money to the repo market ahead of an upcoming long holiday and public share offers by a bank and two firms have also caused cash withdrawal from the bourse.

A religious holiday between April 17-21 will be followed by an official holiday on April 23. The government has declared April 22 holiday for state offices, but it is not yet known if the markets will be closed.
"I expect this trend to continue next week although there may be a recovery one or two days before the holiday," said Mehmet Muderrisoglu from Taib investment.
The Exchange has a two-day settlement rule which usually prompts buying ahead of holidays.

Of the 244 shares traded, falls outdid rises by 150 to 46 and 48 were stable. The IMKB Industrial lost 0.99 percent to 1,500, the IMKB Services eased 0.42 percent to 1,414 and the IMKB Financial edged 0.12 percent lower to 1,613.

The most heavily traded shares were those of commercial vehicle producer Anadolu-Isuzu which were listed on Thursday at an opening price of 57,000 lira. They gained 4,000 lira to 74,000 and made up 14 percent of the total turnover.
